---
title: "Urchin Foraging Rates on Kelp at Different Urchin Densities"
subtitle: "Exploring the mutate function in RStudio through investigating urchin laboratory data from the SBC LTER."
format: pdf
---

## Set Up

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# loading in packages 
library(tidyverse) # general use
library(janitor) # cleaning data 
library(here) # data organization 

# reading in data 

# urchin density data from DiFiore et al. 2021
urchin <- read.csv(here("data","mesocosm_density_data.csv"))
```

## Cleaning Data & Using Mutate Function

```{r}
#| label: urchin-data-cleaning
# create new object urchin_clean
urchin_clean <- urchin |> 
  # clean column names
  clean_names() |>
  # keeping first unique row for each unique combination 
  # used to remove repetative data from each individual urchin
  distinct(trial_id, tank, .keep_all = TRUE) |> 
  # filter for trials with no mortality 
  filter(mortality == 0) |> 
  # mutate p_r to show the different species of urchins
  rename(species = p_r) |> 
  mutate(species = case_when(
    species == "p" ~ "Purple urchin",
    species == "r" ~ "Red urchin"
    )) |> 
  # mutate kelp_in and kelp_out columns to the kelp foraging rate of the urchins
  mutate(
    rate_per_urchin = (kelp_in - kelp_out) / total_time / urchin_density) |> 
  mutate(
    kelp_consumption_rate = (kelp_in - kelp_out) / total_time) |> 
  # select for desired columns of interest 
  select(urchin_density, rate_per_urchin, species, total_time, kelp_consumption_rate) 
```

## Visualization 

```{r}
#| label: visualization-of-urchin-density-rate

# base plot 
ggplot(data = urchin_clean,
  # x-axis urchin density, y-axis urchin consumption rate
  # color by species 
       mapping = aes(x = urchin_density,
                     y = rate_per_urchin,
                     color = species)) + 
  # first layer: geom_point
  geom_point(shape = 20,
             alpha = 0.5,
             size = 4) + 
  # separating by species 
  facet_wrap(~species) +
  # customizing colors
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Purple urchin" = "mediumorchid4",
    "Red urchin" = "firebrick")) +
  # labeling axes and adding title 
  labs(x = "Urchin density (per tank)",
       y = "Kelp consumed per urchin (grams/hour)",
       title = "Urchin foragaing rate on kelp across different urchin densities") + 
  # adding custom theme 
  theme_minimal() +
  # removing legend
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
#| label: visualization-of-kelp-consumption-rate

# base plot 
ggplot(data = urchin_clean,
  # x-axis urchin density, y-axis urchin consumption rate
  # color by species 
       mapping = aes(x = urchin_density,
                     y = kelp_consumption_rate,
                     color = species)) + 
  # first layer: geom_point
  geom_point(shape = 20,
             alpha = 0.5,
             size = 4) + 
    # separating by species 
  facet_wrap(~species) +
    # customizing colors
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Purple urchin" = "mediumorchid4",
    "Red urchin" = "firebrick")) +
  labs(x = "Urchin density (urchins per tank)",
       y = "Kelp consumption rate (grams/hour)",
       title = "Kelp consumption versus urchin density") + 
  # adding custom theme 
  theme_minimal() +
  # removing legend
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Data Citation
DiFiore, B, M. Rennick, J. Curtis, D. Reed, A. Stier. 2021. SBC LTER: Sea urchin foraging rates on giant kelp ver 1. Environmental Data Initiative. https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/6af4cc3b0e63b887baf1ae9201e1cd1d. Accessed 2026-10-16.
